---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Productive Net-Equity Deleveraging
EXPRESSION: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at))), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Net equity issuance used alongside debt retirement predicts higher returns when asset productivity improves.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Netting repurchases from stock issuance removes equity churn and isolates genuine substitution of creditor claims with new outside equity. This targeted financing measurement should sharpen the productive recapitalization mechanism without changing its validated operating conditioner.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Dividend-Floor Cash Drawdown
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(dvc, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), RATIO(oancf, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Maintaining a high dividend floor predicts lower returns when operating cash profitability is far below its recent peak.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The historical minimum dividend intensity measures the binding payout floor rather than a generic dividend level. Centering the cash drawdown creates an explicit comparison between committed payers in severe drawdowns and committed payers whose cash generation remains near its peak, addressing the prior slope-versus-portfolio disagreement.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Abnormal Deleveraging at Cash Drawdown
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), RATIO(oancf, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Unusually large debt retirement predicts lower returns when it occurs during a severe operating-cash drawdown.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Positioning debt retirement within the firm’s own history isolates exceptional deleveraging events rather than the generally favorable cross-sectional debt-reduction effect. The signed drawdown conditioner contrasts potentially forced deleveraging with similarly unusual retirement undertaken near normal cash capacity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Volatility-Conditioned Dividend Rigidity
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dvc, prstkc), at)), IND_ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Dividend-heavy payout policies predict lower returns when cash flows are volatile and relatively higher returns when cash flows are stable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This isolates the adverse dividend-rigidity side of payout-policy matching rather than using a symmetric financing-mix score whose portfolio evidence was strong but cross-sectional slope was weak. Centered cash volatility places stable dividend-heavy firms in the favorable tail and volatile dividend-heavy firms in the adverse tail.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Equity-Funded Dividend-Floor Defense
EXPRESSION: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(dvc, at), 3))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), at), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Equity issuance used while defending a persistent dividend floor predicts lower returns when post-dividend operating cash is weak.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The dividend floor distinguishes a rigid commitment from an incidental current-year distribution, making equity issuance more plausibly related to payout preservation. Weak residual cash then identifies firms diluting shareholders to avoid resetting that commitment rather than financing productive operations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Weak-Cash Dividend-Cut Dilution
EXPRESSION: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1))), IND_RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Simultaneous dividend retrenchment and share-count dilution predict lower returns when operating cash profitability is weak.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: A dividend reduction and dilution are two distinct financing confirmations that internal and external funding conditions have deteriorated. The weak-cash conditioner separates genuine financing distress from firms that cut dividends or issue shares despite otherwise strong operating capacity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Productive Net-Equity Deleveraging---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a one-term cosmetic edit of the archived "Productive Equity-Funded Deleveraging" (gross sstk replaced by sstk−prstkc, identical MIN structure and identical sales-trend conditioner), and netting repurchases also drags in the well-known net-share-issuance anomaly whose sign runs opposite to the stated positive expectation.

---CRITIQUE Dividend-Floor Cash Drawdown---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The re-centering of the drawdown conditioner is a defensible response to the earlier slope/alpha disagreement, but TS_MIN of a highly persistent dividend ratio is nearly collinear with the MA(dvc/at,3) already used in "Dividend Burden at Cash Drawdown," so most of the proposal is a renormalization rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Abnormal Deleveraging at Cash Drawdown---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: It is a close relative of the archived "Cash-Drawdown Forced Deleveraging" (which already produced a slope opposite to the hypothesized sign), and the only real innovation — within-firm TS_RANK of net retirement over a 3-period window — yields a coarse three-valued variable unlikely to isolate "exceptional" deleveraging cleanly.

---CRITIQUE Volatility-Conditioned Dividend Rigidity---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Since dvc−prstkc is exactly the negation of the archived "Volatility-Matched Payout Flexibility" payout term and the expected sign is flipped in tandem, this is the same signal with the rank/z-score roles swapped, i.e., a rediscovery rather than a new test.

---CRITIQUE Equity-Funded Dividend-Floor Defense---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Identical in structure and conditioner to the archived "Equity-Funded Dividend Strain" with only dvc/at swapped for its 3-year minimum, a substitution that changes little for sticky dividend payers and does not constitute a substantively different mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Weak-Cash Dividend-Cut Dilution---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The specific conjunction of dividend retrenchment with share-count dilution under weak operating cash has not been tested in the archive and is internally consistent with a negative sign, though it is close in spirit to the existing weak-cash payout-switch family and largely stacks three individually known distress/issuance predictors.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Post-Buyback Cash Realization
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Prior repurchase spending predicts higher returns when subsequently validated by improving operating cash profitability.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Lagging the repurchase separates the financing decision from the later quality realization, testing management’s information rather than contemporaneous firm quality. Repurchasers with improving cash profitability occupy the favorable tail, while repurchasers followed by cash deterioration form an economically distinct adverse tail.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Borrowing-After-Dividend-Cut Stress
EXPRESSION: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1)))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Simultaneous long-term borrowing and dividend retrenchment predict lower returns when gross margins are weak.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Borrowing despite cutting dividends indicates that payout relief is insufficient to close the funding gap. Weak operating margins make the joint financing response more indicative of persistent stress than either debt issuance or a dividend cut considered separately.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Weak-Margin Maturity Shortening
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(dlc, 1), dltis), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: A financing shift toward current debt predicts lower returns when persistent gross margins are weak.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Current-debt growth in excess of long-term issuance captures maturity shortening and greater rollover exposure, rather than total external financing. Conditioning on margin level replaces the unsuccessful stable-margin maturity-extension hypothesis with an adverse funding structure that is especially risky when operating buffers are thin.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cash-Backed Payout Expansion
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Increases in total shareholder payouts predict higher returns when backed by persistent operating cash profitability and lower returns when cash quality is weak.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The financing leg measures a payout-policy expansion rather than its level, stability, or allocation between dividends and repurchases. A signed cash-quality conditioner distinguishes credible distribution of surplus cash from payout increases that may require subsequent external financing.

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Post-Deleveraging Margin Recovery
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(DELTA(RATIO(ib, sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Prior net debt retirement predicts higher returns when followed by improving operating margins.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This tests whether deleveraging precedes an operating turnaround, rather than pairing debt retirement with another contemporaneous level or trend. Margin improvement validates that creditor reduction restored operating flexibility, while continued margin deterioration identifies forced or ineffective deleveraging.
